title: A Little Princess
author: Frances Hodgson Burnett
openingText:
One dark winter day, a little girl with an unusual face was riding slowly along London's broad streets in a cab beside her father. Yellow fog lay so thick and heavy over the city that the street lamps had been lit, and gaslight shone from the shop windows just as it did at night.

Her feet were tucked beneath her, and she leaned into her father, who had an arm around her. As she watched the people passing outside the window, her wide eyes held a strange, thoughtful look that seemed to belong to someone much older.
about:
Sara Crewe arrives at a London boarding school as a wealthy seven-year-old. She loves books, invents stories and tries to treat other people kindly. When news of her father's death and the loss of his fortune arrives on her eleventh birthday, Miss Minchin makes her work for the school and sleep in an attic.

First published as a novel in 1905, A Little Princess follows Sara through hunger, loneliness, friendship and an unexpected change of fortune. Her imagination helps her endure hardship, but food, warmth and practical kindness matter just as much. The story also exposes the way money changes how adults treat a child. Its depictions of class and colonial India reflect the world in which Burnett wrote.

whyItMatters.title: Imagination and endurance
whyItMatters.body: Sara imagines herself as a princess and invents stories for her friends. Watch when this helps her bear hardship and when exhaustion and hunger defeat it. Her imagination is powerful, but it cannot replace food or protection.

whyItMatters.title: Kindness and power
whyItMatters.body: Miss Minchin's treatment of Sara changes when the money disappears. Becky receives little consideration because she is a servant. The novel asks readers to notice how wealth and social position affect who receives respect and care.

whyItMatters.title: Sharing what you have
whyItMatters.body: Sara shares stories, comfort and food even when she has little herself. The bakery episode connects a small act of generosity with later practical help. The ending invites a question: what should someone do with the power that money brings?

angleCards.title: Sara's imagination
angleCards.text: Follow the stories Sara tells herself and others, and notice when they help and when they are not enough.
angleCards.angleObjective: I'm reading A Little Princess to explore how imagination helps Sara endure hardship and connect with others.

angleCards.title: Money and treatment
angleCards.text: Compare how Miss Minchin and the other characters treat Sara before and after she loses her money.
angleCards.angleObjective: I'm reading A Little Princess to examine how money and status influence care, respect and power.

angleCards.title: Sara and Becky
angleCards.text: Follow the friendship between a pupil and a servant, including the differences that remain between their lives.
angleCards.angleObjective: I'm reading A Little Princess to understand Sara and Becky's friendship across class differences.

angleCards.title: Being a princess
angleCards.text: Notice what Sara means by calling herself a princess, especially when she is hungry, angry or able to help someone.
angleCards.angleObjective: I'm reading A Little Princess to follow Sara's changing understanding of generosity, dignity and being a princess.

cast.name: Sara Crewe
cast.description: Seven when she arrives at Miss Minchin's school, Sara is thoughtful, well read and fluent in French. After her father's death she must work and live in the attic. She tries to hold on to her idea of how a princess should behave.

cast.name: Captain Crewe
cast.description: A young English officer in India and Sara's only surviving parent. He loves and indulges her. His investment in diamond mines and his friendship with Tom Carrisford shape the events that leave Sara without protection.

cast.name: Miss Minchin
cast.description: She runs the boarding school with her sister Amelia. She values Sara's wealth and accomplishments, then treats her harshly when she can no longer pay. Her concern for appearances repeatedly conflicts with the child's welfare.

cast.name: Becky
cast.description: A young servant worn out by hard work. Sara befriends her after finding her asleep in Sara's own room. Becky already sleeps in an attic next to the one Sara later occupies; their friendship helps both girls endure hunger and loneliness.

cast.name: Mr. Carrisford
cast.description: Captain Crewe's friend and business partner, now ill and burdened by guilt. He searches for Crewe's daughter with the help of Mr. Carmichael. He moves next door to Sara without knowing her identity.

cast.name: Ram Dass
cast.description: Mr. Carrisford's Indian servant. An escaped monkey leads him to Sara's attic. He learns about her hardship and helps arrange the secret gifts that transform the room, before either he or his employer knows who she really is.
